The macro-micro modeling approach begins with a sample scale model to identify the location mostly prone to failure and obtain the deformation history of the boundaries of that location. The calculated deformation history will then be used to drive a microstructure-based macro-models where the material microstructure and microscale properties are considered. The project began with phase I effort of building a framework of macro-micro three point (3-P) bending test and clinch test of Aural-5 HPDC Al alloy (Al7SiMgMn) in both as-cast and e-coated conditions. In the phase I work which has just been completed, the macro-micro modeling frameworks have been constructed for both the 3-P bending and clinch tests and applied to the Aural-5 HPDC alloy plates with 2.9mm thickness in both conditions. The tensile tests of the alloys in both conditions were obtained and flow behavior extracted were then used in the macro and micro model. The microstructures of the as-cast alloy were characterized and used in the micro-model construction. The microstructures consist of primary Al- dendrites and Al/Si eutectics. The e-coating process will not influence the microstructures but promotes the nano-precipitates formation in the Al-dendrites. The 3-P bending tests of the alloys in both conditions were performed to be used to calibrate the fracture strains of both the Al-dendrites and Al/Si eutectics in the aural-5 alloys in both as-cast and e-coated conditions. The clinch test of only the e-coated aural-5 was performed. The fracture strains determined from the 3-P bending tests and modeling for the e-coated alloys is applied to the micro-model of the clinch test and simulation calculated critical displacement is within the range of data of experimental measurements. The phase II project effort involved the utilization of the knowledge learned in phase I to establish the quantitative correlation between the microstructure characteristics and the riveting performance, which will be further used to guide the optimization of HPDC Al alloy microstructure with different casting conditions and e-coating process to achieve sufficient rivetability to join large thin-wall HPDC alloys. 2. STATEMENT OF OBJECTIVES The purpose of this project is to extend and validate an existing finite element code, which is based on the Contractor developed macro-micro multi-scale modeling approach, to numerically simulate the three-point bending and clinch test and study the influences of material microstructural characteristics and phase properties on the rivetability. The macro-micro modeling approach begins with a sample scale model and identify the location, which is mostly prone to failure, the deformation history of the boundaries of that location calculated will be used to drive a microstructure-based sub-models where the material microstructure and microscale properties are considered. Using this approach, the wrap-bending failure for two Al alloys are correctly predicted for the first time. 5 The project began with a phase I effort of building a framework of macro-micro three point bending test and clinch test of Al7SiMgMn HPDC alloy in the as-cast and e-coated conditions.
